claims.text: Iran called for Qatar to release three Iranian pilots it stated were captured after two fighter jets were hit by air defences at the start of the US-Iran war.
Iranian Brig Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh stated in a letter to the ICRC that pilots Javad Salehi, Abdul Majid Dashtian, and Imran Behroshian had been held captive by Qatar for six months.
Bagherzadeh stated that the body of a fourth pilot, Majid Kazemi, was returned after he was killed during the combat mission on March 2, 2026.
Qatar denied Iran's allegations regarding the detention of the pilots, describing them as misleading statements.
Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al-Ansari confirmed Qatari air defence forces engaged two Iranian warplanes in March after they breached Qatari airspace without responding to warnings.
In early March 2026, Qatar's Defence Ministry reported shooting down two Iranian Sukhoi Su-24 bombers during an attack on Al Udeid Air Base.
US President Donald Trump stated in New York that Iran was being 'very badly defeated' and suggested he would soon declare the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the Strait of Hormuz 'cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier'.
Kazem Gharibabadi stated on X that 'The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
UAE state-owned oil giant ADNOC reported that one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday night.
A US defense official told NPR that the aircraft carrier USS George Washington is en route to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao stated that the deployment of the USS Lincoln was extended because the conflict with Iran demanded it.
The USS Abraham Lincoln has spent more than 240 consecutive days at sea during its Middle East deployment.
A 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off the island of Flores in eastern Indonesia shortly before 05:00 local time on Saturday at a depth of 15km.
At least 47 people were reported killed across several provinces in eastern Indonesia following the earthquake.
Authorities lifted an initial tsunami warning approximately three hours after the quake when no significant sea level rise was detected.
The 7.7-magnitude earthquake off Flores was followed by more than 230 aftershocks, including a major tremor measuring 6.1.
A separate 6.9-magnitude earthquake struck Sumatra at a depth of 172km within the same 24-hour period.
Rescue officials in the port town of Maumere found 20 people dead, six severely injured, and two trapped under rubble following building collapses and landslides.
Landslides in Ende regency severed the Trans-Flores highway, a 435-mile mountain road.
The United States Geological Survey placed the epicentre of the 7.7-magnitude quake 68 kilometres northwest of the city of Ende at a depth of 10 kilometres.
Sixteen bodies were recovered from a landslide site in the village of Reok in the Manggarai region.
The Indonesian government dispatched 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the disaster region.
European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the EU's Copernicus Earth observation satellites to support search and rescue efforts.
Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on Saturday killed at least 11 people and wounded 19 others.
Seven people, including three children and two women, were killed in an Israeli airstrike on a house in the village of Ansar.
The Israeli military reported killing Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force unit, during the strike in Ansar.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam posted on X that the civilians killed in Ansar were not 'military infrastructure'.
The Israeli Prime Minister's office stated that a Hezbollah attack on the Ali al-Taher Ridge seriously injured three Israeli soldiers prior to the retaliatory strike.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that the Israeli strikes sent a clear message regarding US-led framework negotiations.
Hezbollah released a statement demanding an end to 'humiliating' peace negotiations with Israel.
Netanyahu spokesman Doron Spielman stated that the latest Israeli strikes should jumpstart negotiations and make them much more serious.
Lebanese official news agency NNA reported that Israeli forces detonated several homes in the border town of Bint Jbeil.
Supporters of the Taliban gathered in central Kabul on Saturday, August 15, to celebrate five years of Taliban rule.
Taliban members performed the traditional Pashtun attan dance in a Kabul public square during anniversary events.
The Taliban regained power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021, following the withdrawal of foreign NATO forces.
Shortly after taking power, the Taliban imposed an indefinite ban on girls' education beyond the sixth grade and later suspended higher education for women.
U.N. Women stated that Afghanistan has systematically dismantled the rights of half its population over the past five years.
Taliban deputy broadcasting minister Molvi Hayatullah Mahajar Farahi stated that the administration has delivered security, currency stability, and infrastructure improvements over five years.
Hundreds of Afghan Special Immigrant Visa holders residing in the US received notices from the federal government stating the approval basis for their visas was revoked or denied.
The US State Department has issued 160,000 Special Immigrant Visas to Afghans since the program's authorization in 2009.
Moroccan security forces detained 111 migrants near the town of Fnideq while preventing a mass attempt to cross into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.
Moroccan police used tear gas to disperse groups of migrants gathered on hills near the border.
Italy suspended Schengen free-movement arrangements with Spain and introduced border checks after a major migration surge into Ceuta in late July.
More than 72,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta during a major influx on July 30, resulting in at least 96 deaths.
Spain deployed over 500 additional police officers to Ceuta, bringing the total security presence in the exclave to more than 1,600 personnel.
Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska stated that around 5,000 migrants remained in Ceuta.
False posts on social media claiming the border would open for the Assumption holiday spurred migrants to gather near the Ceuta border.
Moroccan news portal Le360 reported that up to 294 people, including 46 Moroccans, were arrested during Saturday's border security operation.
A severe wildfire destroyed a third of the High Fens natural reserve in eastern Belgium, leading to the evacuation of two nearby villages.
Belgium activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism to request international firefighting aircraft and helicopters.
Local authorities in Landes, south-western France, evacuated 650 residents due to a reignited forest fire.
The wildfire in Belgium's High Fens park had scorched at least 16 square kilometres by Saturday afternoon.
Wallonia regional spokesperson Nicolas Yernaux called the High Fens blaze the largest wildfire in Belgium's recent history.
A violent coastal wildfire in Croatia killed at least one person and injured approximately 42 others.
Local Belgian authorities reported that the High Fens fire expanded from 80 hectares on Friday to over 2,700 hectares by late Saturday.
French authorities detained 474 people, including 183 minors, on suspicion of starting wildfires since July 1.
More than 2,000 people evacuated their homes in western Germany as a wildfire in the Hürtgen forest approached the village of Gey.
Unexploded Second World War ordnance detonated during the Hürtgen forest fire in Germany, forcing firefighters to keep their distance.
Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra issued a letter on August 15 apologizing to law students for any hurt caused by his recent directives or words.
The Bar Council of India had previously ordered state bar councils to defer the advocate enrolment of NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch before withdrawing the directive.
NALSAR students had objected to inviting CJI Surya Kant to their convocation over his remarks regarding a petition on alleged police brutality in Delhi.
CJI Surya Kant criticized the Bar Council of India's intervention, stating that peaceful student protests were a matter strictly between him and the students.
Around 450 NALSAR students had submitted six representations to their university administration asking to reconsider the CJI's convocation invitation.
The Supreme Court restrained the BCI and state bar councils from pursuing any punitive or criminal action against students and faculty over the NALSAR row.
Graduating students from NLSIU Bengaluru released a statement condemning the BCI's actions against NALSAR graduates and demanding an unconditional apology.
A petition filed in the Supreme Court requested structural reforms to the Bar Council of India, including fixed term limits for its chairman.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered his 13th Independence Day address from the Red Fort, introducing a seven-point reform plan named Saptadhara.
For the first time in 80 years, Vande Mataram preceded the national anthem during the Red Fort Independence Day ceremony.
PM Modi mentioned the youth of India approximately 50 times during his 75-minute Independence Day speech.
PM Modi announced free online coaching for competitive exams and an AI skilling program aimed at training one crore youth in the coming year.
PM Modi stated that India has set a target to achieve 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 following the passage of the SHANTI Act.
Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge skipped the Red Fort Independence Day event for the second consecutive year over seating protocol disagreements.
PM Modi stated from the Red Fort that 'dimagi Naxals' are threatening Indian society and called for them to be 'found and isolated'.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh criticized PM Modi's 'dimaagi naxals' remark, calling it a sign of desperation.
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal criticized PM Modi following a brief speech pause, describing him as 'an under-confident, nervous and shaky Prime Minister'.
Student protesters under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch announced plans to gherao Chief Minister Hemant Soren's residence in Ranchi on August 20 to demand his resignation.
Protesting students conducted a 'Tiranga Yatra' march from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi on Independence Day.
The student agitation demanding reforms and transparency in Jharkhand recruitment examinations entered its 22nd day on Saturday.
JLKM leader Devendra Mahto alleged that police forcibly prevented him from leaving Sadar Hospital in Ranchi to participate in the protest march.
Former Jharkhand Chief Minister Champai Soren questioned why the state government has been reluctant to recommend a CBI probe into exam irregularities.
Student leader Ravindra Paswan issued an ultimatum to the Jharkhand government to address their demands by August 18.
Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured students during his Independence Day address that allegations of recruitment irregularities would be investigated impartially.
Protest leader Devendra Nath Mahto has been conducting a hunger strike for 14 days over the recruitment examination controversy.
